initial.parent_question: Construct two positive physical gaps g1,g2 with g1+g2=3n/4, for every real n>0 and L>3, in the comparison representation.
initial.current_strategy: Use the two-scale proposed alternative whose junction displacement is -3/4.
initial.scientific_context: The parent matching requirement is g1+g2=3n/4. A previously used narrow representation is unavailable, but other representations have not been excluded. Positivity of actual gaps, not the sign of a junction coordinate, is the physical condition.
initial.new_contribution: The proposed alternative has g1=n/4-3n/(4L), g2=n/2+3n/(4L). The downstream consumer has now been qualified: each physical gap must be at least n/3, not merely positive.
initial.assignment: Determine what survives this qualification and whether the proposed alternative serves the parent interface. Continue with a justified mathematical decision; do not assume the new qualification invalidates the parent problem.

initial.parent_question: Replace a continuous averaging functional by small positive finite evaluations, retaining exact polynomial information.
initial.scientific_context: The functional is I(f)=(1/pi) integral_0^pi f(7/2+(3/2)cos(theta)) dtheta. Existing formulas give I(f)=f(7/2) for deg f<=1; and I(f)=[f(7/2-3sqrt(2)/4)+f(7/2+3sqrt(2)/4)]/2 for deg f<=3. These are exact on their stated degree ranges, not arbitrary-function identities.
initial.new_contribution: A third exact formula is [f(7/2-3sqrt(3)/4)+f(7/2)+f(7/2+3sqrt(3)/4)]/3 for deg f<=5. All nodes lie in (2,5) and all weights are positive.
initial.assignment: Derive a four-evaluation formula of the greatest exactness you can justify. Preserve any unexpected reusable structure with its proof and limitations, even if it goes beyond the requested instance.

archive.title: Single-junction multiplier convention
archive.body: The sufficient forcing condition in this theorem is delta-1<=1/512, where delta=D/C. The theorem uses this literal multiplicative ratio, not a parameter inferred by the same informal name in another record. All other hypotheses remain independent.

initial.parent_question: Determine a justified growing-order positive-definite range.
initial.current_strategy: Extend a fixed-order limiting construction to a specified finite-parameter range.
initial.scientific_context: For integers r,n>=1, H_(r,n) is diagonal with entries 1-j^2/n, 1<=j<=r. For every fixed r, H_(r,n) tends to the identity as n tends to infinity and is eventually positive definite. Fixed-order limiting rank is already established.
initial.new_contribution: A proposed composition asserts that the limiting statement proves positive definiteness simultaneously for every 1<=r<=floor(n^(2/3)), once n is sufficiently large.
initial.assignment: Determine the exact reach of the proposal and any useful alternative conclusion. Preserve valid limiting information while keeping its quantifiers separate from a finite uniform assertion.

initial.parent_question: Determine what exact information the new scalar representation makes available to retained finite-dimensional constructions.
initial.current_strategy: Bound a scalar derivative on the positive half-line.
initial.scientific_context: The scalar derivative problem is selected. No assertion about all finite interpolation tables has been established for the current representation.
initial.new_contribution: For every z>0, F(z)=1/z+2/(z+1)+1/(z+3). This exact representation is valid on the whole positive half-line. It is not a large-z expansion.
initial.assignment: Investigate the consequences of this representation for the Mission's mathematical questions, including a qualified consequential use if available. Read exact backing and do not infer a quantitative condition number from qualitative positivity.

archive.title: Sample-energy table
archive.body: For positive weights w_l and real sample functions v_i(t_l), the table G_ij=sum_l w_l v_i(t_l)v_j(t_l) obeys c^T G c=sum_l w_l(sum_i c_i v_i(t_l))^2>=0. It is positive definite exactly when the sample row vectors are linearly independent. Rank is at most the number of samples. For positive-definite G, the energy (1/2)c^T G c-b^T c has a unique minimizer G^-1 b for every real b. No condition-number estimate follows from these statements alone.

archive.title: Secant interpolation energy
archive.body: For distinct positive sites z_1,...,z_k and a differentiable scalar function g, this consumer forms D_ij=(g(z_i)-g(z_j))/(z_j-z_i) for i!=j and D_ii=-g'(z_i). The unresolved use is a unique minimizer of (1/2)c^T D c-b^T c for arbitrary b. A negative derivative on its own does not establish that property.

archive.title: Positive resolvent slope shortcut
archive.body: The diagonal signs -g'(z_i)>0 alone do not make the secant table positive definite. For example the symmetric matrix with diagonal 1 and off-diagonal 2 is indefinite. This is an obstruction to the diagonal-only shortcut, not to every representation.

archive.title: Rational function expansion
archive.body: A finite large-z expansion of a rational function does not identify its values or divided differences at all positive sites. A truncated expansion is not an exact interpolation certificate.
